paragraphs: Children in care in Bristol are looked after by carers approved by Bristol City Council's own service, Foster with Bristol City Council, and by the independent fostering agencies listed on this page. The council says many children come into its care each year, for reasons that include family breakdown, a parent's illness, neglect, domestic abuse or drug and alcohol misuse at home. Some stay in foster care for a short time and others until they are ready to live on their own.

The council names the groups of children it most needs homes for: babies, teenagers, brothers and sisters who need to stay together, unaccompanied asylum-seeking children, and children with additional needs. If you could offer a home to one of these groups, it is worth saying so early in any conversation with a fostering service.

Bristol pays every carer a weekly Level 1 allowance for each child, from £181.95 for a child aged up to 2 to £296.16 for a young person aged 16 or 17, and the same rate continues for young people who stay on after 18 under Staying Put. Carers approved at Level 2 receive an extra £160 a week per child, and at Level 3 an extra £250. Our Bristol allowance page lists the birthday, festival and holiday payments too.

The council's fostering team offers an informal chat to anyone thinking about fostering. Speaking to the council and to two or three of the agencies below, and asking each about training, support and pay, is a good way to find the right fit.

sources.title: Our children who need fostering (Foster with Bristol City Council)
